## Expressions
:::{style='font-size:80%'}

$$ \log\det M[\phi]=\log\det(\mathbb{1}_{N_x}+\underbrace{F_k(N_t-1).F_k(N_t-2)\ldots F_k(0)}_{\mathrm{``sausage\ 1"}})\quad;\quad F_k(t)\equiv \underbrace{e^{\tilde\kappa}}_{\mathrm{dense}}. \underbrace{e^{i\phi_t(x)}}_{\mathrm{diagonal}} \quad;\quad \tilde\kappa=\kappa\frac{\beta}{N_t}$$

$$\partial_{\phi_t(x)} \log\det M[\phi]= \left\{f_k(t+1).f_k(t+2)\ldots f_k(N_t-1).\left[\mathbb{1}_{N_x}+\underbrace{f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)}_{\mathrm{``sausage\ 2"}}\right]^{-1}.f_k(0)\ldots f_k(t) \right\}_{x,x} $$
$$ f_k(t)=F_k^{-1}(k)=e^{-i\phi_t(x)}.e^{-\tilde\kappa}$$

+ Note:  $[\mathrm{sausage\ 2}]^{-1}=\mathrm{sausage\ 1}$
:::

## Stabilizing $\log\det M$

:::{style='font-size:70%'}

+ Express $F_k(t)=e^{\tilde\kappa}.e^{i\phi_t}=U.\underbrace{D_{\tilde\kappa}}_{\mathrm{diagonal}}.\underbrace{V.e^{i\phi_t}}_{\equiv V(t)}\equiv U.D_{\tilde\kappa}.V(t)$
  - Note that $U.V=\mathbb{1}_{N_x}$ ***and*** $V(t).V^\dagger (t)=\mathbb{1}_{N_x}$

+ Initial SVD of sausage
  $$ F_k(N_t-1).F_k(N_t-2)\ldots F_k(0)=U.\underbrace{D_{\tilde\kappa}.V(N_t-1).U.D_{\tilde\kappa}}_{=u.d.v}.V(N_t-2)\ldots U.D_{\tilde\kappa}.V(0)$$

+ Recursively perform SVD^[One can also do a different decomposition, like QR.  For these notes I only assume SVD. Only slight changes would be required for a different decomposition.] on expressions of the form $D.V(t).U.D =u.d.v$ until one arrives at
  $$ \mathbb{1}_{N_x}+u.d.v = u.(\underbrace{u^\dagger v^\dagger+d}_{q.r}).v \quad\quad (=\mathbb{1}_{N_x}+\mathrm{sausage})$$

+ Final expression for $\log\det M$
  $$ \log\det M = \log\det\left(u.q.r.v\right) =\log\det(u.q)+\log\det(v)+\sum_x\log r_{x,x}$$
:::

## Stabilizing $\partial\log\det M$

:::{style='font-size:80%'}

+ Key feature here is the construction of $[\mathbb{1}+f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)]^{-1}$

+ Express $f_k(t)=e^{-i\phi_t}.e^{-\tilde\kappa}=\underbrace{e^{-i\phi_t}.U}_{\equiv U(t)}.\underbrace{D_{\tilde\kappa}}_{\mathrm{diagonal}}.V\equiv U(t).D_{\tilde\kappa}.V$ 

+ As before, we construct the sausage via recursive decomposition 
  $$ \mathbb{1}+f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)=\mathbb{1}+u.d.v=u.(\underbrace{u^\dagger v^\dagger+d}_{q.r}).v =u.q.r.v$$

+ Then we have
  $$ [\mathbb{1}+f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)]^{-1}=v^\dagger.r^{-1}.q^\dagger.u^\dagger $$
  
+ Though there is an inverse to calculate, $r^{-1}$, this matrix is triangular and so this should not be that bad


:::

## Strategy for calculating $\partial_{\phi_t}\log\det M$

:::{style='font-size:80%'}

+ Assume we can calculate $\mathcal{N}_k\equiv[f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)].[\mathbb{1}+f_k(0)\ldots f_k(N_t-1)]^{-1}$

+ Then 
  $$
  \begin{align}
  \dot\pi(0)&=f_k(0)^{-1}.\mathcal{N}_k.f_k(0) = F_k(0).\mathcal{N}_k.f_k(0)\\
  \dot\pi(1)&=F_k(1).\dot\pi(0).f_k(1)\\
  \vdots\\
  \dot\pi(t)&=F_k(t).\dot\pi(t-1).f_k(t)\\
  \vdots
  \end{align}
  $$
  
:::{.r-stack}
The calculation of $\dot\pi(t)$ should be stable, since at any one time we are always multiplying matrices with matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ or less.
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
## But this assumes that we have calculated $\mathcal{N}_k$ accurately!!!
:::
  
:::

## Testing in the non-interacting limit on the 4-site hex (w/ PBCs)

:::{style='font-size:80%'}

+ In the non-interacting limit we have $\phi_t(x)=0\quad\forall\  x,t$.  

+ We can compare to exact analytic results
